appendices.title: The Missing Row and the Last Verified Statistic

balance.argument_a: The Recovery keeps the paper's reported circle at its true size (52 members, matching what the lab has always claimed about this ego-network) and produces a number for every member -- but that one number (the reconstructed degree for the missing member) is only ever an estimate built from a five-week-old statistic, and it is exactly as fabricated, structurally, as any other estimated data point: 1 of 52 members (1.923%) is not an exact, verified value.
balance.argument_b: The Clean Drop never reports a single fabricated number -- every value in the 51-member dataset is exact and verified -- but it silently shrinks the circle from 52 to 51 members in every downstream statistic, so 1 of 52 members (1.923%) is not represented at all. On the case's own primary metric (share of the circle represented by an exact, known value), this is mathematically identical to Option A's compromise: both options touch exactly one member, neither more nor less.
balance.margin_basis: 51/52 (members with an exact, known degree count) computed identically for A (the estimated member is not exact) and B (the dropped member is not represented) -- see sensitivity_model.py. The two options are a genuine structural tie on this metric, by construction, for any value of the case's one stated assumption (Appendix C, MA1).
